steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on the tilted exponential (TEXP) layer, a communication-theory-inspired way to make neural networks more robust. Cover the background on data augmentation, the matched-filtering idea, how the layer works, and a summary of our experiments.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
1. Standard deep nets lack robustness; data augmentation is the usual fix
2. Our idea: borrow detection/estimation theory from communication systems
3. The TEXP layer: learning and inference
4. Summary of experiments and results

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Robustness problem
- standard training lacks robustness: noise, distribution shifts, adversarial attacks
- most common fix: data augmentation
- adversarial training: augments with adversarial examples for current network parameters; one of most effective defenses
- other augmentation types help against natural corruptions

2. Communication-theory idea
- complementary to data augmentation
- detection and estimation theory, success in wireless communication
- receiver matches incoming signal against signal templates, one per message
- Gaussian noise: correlating against templates (matched filtering) maximizes SNR
- posterior of each transmitted signal = softmax of suitably scaled matched filter outputs
- apply to enhance SNR in a NN layer via neuronal competition during learning and inference; focus on first layer

3. TEXP layer
- no known set of messages/symbols; learn weights matched to incoming patterns, so a fraction of neurons fire strongly for each strong input
- tilted exponential objective = ML estimation of matched filter templates under Gaussian "data noise" model (Sec. 3)
- inference: tilted softmax replaces batch norm = posterior probabilities of competing templates (neurons)
- data noise variable: smaller in training with clean data, bigger in inference for out of distribution "noise"
- name: tilted exponential (TEXP) layer (Sec. 4)

4. Results
- geometric insight for simplified models; robustness gains for CNNs on standard image datasets
- CIFAR-10, VGG-16 with TEXP first layer: more robust to noise, common corruptions, mild adversarial perturbations, no data augmentation
- further gains with adversarial training, AugMix, RandAugment, AutoAugment
- preliminary: CIFAR-100 (Wide-ResNet-28-10), ImageNet (ResNet-50)

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
Deep neural networks trained in the standard way are known to not be robust to many kinds of distortions, such as noise, distribution shifts, and adversarial attacks. The most common way to improve robustness is to do data augmentation. For example adversarial training is one of the most effective defenses against adversarial attacks, and it works by augmenting the training data with adversarial examples that are generated for the current realization of the network parameters. Different types of data augmentation have also been shown to improve robustness against natural corruptions effectively.

In this paper we propose a different strategy for enhancing robustness, which is complementary to learning with data augmentation. It is based on detection and estimation theoretic concepts, which have been successful in fields like wireless communication systems. In communication theory, the receiver matches the incoming signal against a number of possible signal templates, and each template corresponds to a different message. When signaling in Gaussian noise, correlating against the signal templates (this is often called matched filtering) maximizes the signal-to-noise ratio. The posterior probability of each possible transmitted signal is then obtained by feeding the matched filter outputs, suitably scaled, to a softmax. We propose to use these ideas to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio in a neural network layer through neuronal competition during learning and inference. Here we focus on the first layer.

3. TEXP layer
- no known set of messages/symbols; learn weights matched to incoming patterns, so a fraction of neurons fire strongly for each strong input
- tilted exponential objective = ML estimation of matched filter templates under Gaussian "data noise" model (Sec. 3)
- inference: tilted softmax replaces batch norm = posterior probabilities of competing templates (neurons)
- data noise variable: smaller in training with clean data, bigger in inference for out of distribution "noise"
- name: tilted exponential (TEXP) layer (Sec. 4)

4. Results
- geometric insight for simplified models; robustness gains for CNNs on standard image datasets
- CIFAR-10, VGG-16 with TEXP first layer: more robust to noise, common corruptions, mild adversarial perturbations, no data augmentation
- further gains with adversarial training, AugMix, RandAugment, AutoAugment
- preliminary: CIFAR-100 (Wide-ResNet-28-10), ImageNet (ResNet-50)

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Deep neural networks trained in the standard way are known to not be robust to many kinds of distortions, such as noise, distribution shifts, and adversarial attacks. The most common way to improve robustness is to do data augmentation. For example adversarial training is one of the most effective defenses against adversarial attacks, and it works by augmenting the training data with adversarial examples that are generated for the current realization of the network parameters. Different types of data augmentation have also been shown to improve robustness against natural corruptions effectively.

In this paper we propose a different strategy for enhancing robustness, which is complementary to learning with data augmentation. It is based on detection and estimation theoretic concepts, which have been successful in fields like wireless communication systems. In communication theory, the receiver matches the incoming signal against a number of possible signal templates, and each template corresponds to a different message. When signaling in Gaussian noise, correlating against the signal templates (this is often called matched filtering) maximizes the signal-to-noise ratio. The posterior probability of each possible transmitted signal is then obtained by feeding the matched filter outputs, suitably scaled, to a softmax. We propose to use these ideas to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio in a neural network layer through neuronal competition during learning and inference. Here we focus on the first layer.

In a neural network, unlike in communication systems, we don't have a known set of messages and transmitted symbols. Instead we want to learn layer weights that are well matched to the set of incoming patterns, so that for each strong input a fraction of neurons fire strongly. To do this we add a tilted exponential objective for the layer. This objective can be interpreted as maximum likelihood estimation of matched filter signal templates under a Gaussian model for “data noise” (see Sec. 3). For inference we replace batch norm with a tilted softmax, which can be interpreted as computing posterior probabilities for competing signal templates that are represented by the neurons. The framework lets us vary the amount of data noise during training (smaller if we train with clean data) and during inference (bigger, to give robustness against out of distribution “noise”). We call a layer designed in this way (see Sec. 4) a tilted exponential (TEXP) layer.

We give geometric insight into TEXP training for simplified models, and then we show enhancements in robustness for CNNs on standard image datasets. Experiments on CIFAR-10 show that if we replace the first layer of a VGG-16 network by a TEXP layer, the network becomes more robust against noise, other common corruptions and mild adversarial perturbations, and this does not require data augmentation. We get additional performance gains when we supplement TEXP with adversarial training and other data augmentation techniques such as AugMix, RandAugment and AutoAugment. We also show that the TEXP approach generalizes to other network architectures and datasets, with promising preliminary experiments on CIFAR-100 (with Wide-ResNet-28-10 as backbone) and ImageNet (ResNet-50 backbone).

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
Standard training of deep neural networks is well known to lack robustness against a variety of distortions, including noise, distribution shifts [1,2], and adversarial attacks [3,4,5]. The most common approach to improving robustness is data augmentation. For example, adversarial training [6], which augments the training data with generated adversarial examples (corresponding to the current realization of the network parameters), is one of the most effective defenses against adversarial attacks. Different types of data augmentation have also been shown to effectively improve robustness against natural corruptions [7,8,9].

In this paper, in a manner complementary to learning with data augmentation, we propose and explore a strategy for enhancing robustness based on detection and estimation theoretic concepts, motivated by their success in fields such as wireless communication systems. In communication theory, the receiver tries to match the incoming signal against a number of possible signal templates, each corresponding to a different message. For signaling in Gaussian noise, correlating against these signal templates, often called matched filtering, maximizes the signal-to-noise ratio, and the posterior probability of each possible transmitted signal is obtained by feeding suitably scaled matched filter outputs to a softmax. We propose to apply these ideas to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio in a neural network layer (here we focus on the first layer) via neuronal competition during learning and inference.

Unlike in communication systems, we do not have a known set of messages and corresponding transmitted symbols. Instead, we seek to learn layer weights which are well matched to the set of incoming patterns, so that for each strong input, a fraction of neurons fire strongly. We do this by adding a tilted exponential objective for the layer, which can be interpreted as maximum likelihood estimation of matched filter signal templates under a Gaussian model for “data noise” (see Sec. 3). For inference, we replace batch norm by a tilted softmax, interpretable as computing posterior probabilities for competing signal templates represented by the neurons. Our framework lets us vary the amount of data noise during training (smaller if training with clean data) and during inference (bigger to provide robustness against out of distribution “noise”). We call a layer designed in this way (see Sec. 4) a tilted exponential (TEXP) layer.

We provide geometric insight into TEXP training for simplified models, and then demonstrate enhancements in robustness for CNNs on standard image datasets. Experiments on CIFAR-10 [10] show that replacing the first layer of a VGG-16 [11] network by a TEXP layer increases robustness against noise, other common corruptions and mild adversarial perturbations without requiring data augmentation. Further performance gains are obtained by supplementing TEXP with adversarial training and other data augmentation techniques such as AugMix [8], RandAugment [12] and AutoAugment [7]. We show that the TEXP approach generalizes to other network architectures and datasets through promising preliminary experiments on CIFAR-100 (with a Wide-ResNet-28-10 backbone) and ImageNet (ResNet-50 backbone).
